title: An integrated all-van der Waals nanobeam laser
authors: Aris Koulas-Simos, Pietro Metuh, Athanasios Paralikis, Kartik Gaur, Maximilian Klonz, Imad Limame, Bárbara L. T. Rosa, Chirag C. Palekar, Battulga Munkhbat, Stephan Reitzenstein
abstract: Transition-metal dichalcogenides offer a promising platform for integrated coherent light sources, yet lasing has largely relied on hybrid photonic architectures without direct quantum-optical verification. Here, we demonstrate an all-van der Waals (all-vdW) high-$β$ nanobeam laser based on a WS$_2$/MoSe$_2$/WS$_{2}$ heterostructure, with the MoSe$_2$ monolayer directly integrated in the WS$_{2}$-based optical resonator for optimal gain-mode overlap. The devices exhibit efficient exciton-cavity coupling at cryogenic temperatures, strongly directional and linearly polarized emission, soft nonlinear input-output characteristics and linewidth narrowing, enabling lasing operation with $β$ near unity. Excitation-power-dependent photon-autocorrelation measurements reveal a transition from thermal to Poissonian photon statistics, with $g_{\mathrm{peak}}^{(2)}(0)$ decreasing from $(1.28\,\pm\,0.09)$ near threshold to $(1.07\,\pm\,0.07)$ above threshold, directly verifying lasing operation. Furthermore, temporal broadening of the autocorrelation uncovers fluctuation-dominated lasing dynamics. These results establish all-vdW heterostructures as a highly attractive platform for integrated coherent light sources in layered-material photonic architectures and scalable quantum-photonic circuits.
summary: The research demonstrates a novel all-van der Waals nanobeam laser built from $	ext{WS}_2/	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WS}_2$ heterostructures. By combining structural engineering with advanced photon correlation measurements, the authors provide strong evidence for high-$ eta$ lasing operation in these layered materials. This establishes a promising platform for scalable quantum-photonic circuits.
main_problem: To demonstrate an all-van der Waals (all-vdW) high-$ eta$ nanobeam laser and establish these heterostructures as a viable platform for integrated coherent light sources.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated lasing in the $	ext{WS}_2/	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WS}_2$ structure, verified by observing a transition to Poissonian photon statistics ($g^{(2)}(0) 	o 1.07$) and characteristic high-$ eta$ nonlinear input-output behavior.
method: The study combines microphotoluminescence ($\mu	ext{PL}$) spectroscopy, finite-element simulations for optical confinement, and crucial quantum-optical measurements using photon autocorrelation ($g^{(2)}$).
model_or_system: The physical system is an all-vdW heterostructure ($	ext{WS}_2/	ext{MoSe}_2/	ext{WS}_2$) patterned into a nanobeam cavity, where the $	ext{MoSe}_2$ monolayer provides optical gain coupled to the surrounding $	ext{WS}_2$-based resonator.
key_observables: Photon autocorrelation function $g^{(2)}(0)$ (decreasing from 1.28 to 1.07), soft S-shaped input-output curve, linewidth narrowing, and strong directional/linear polarization of emission.
important_parameters: High-$ eta$ parameter ($\approx 0.986$), threshold power ($P_{	ext{th}} \approx 9-29 	ext{ kW cm}^{-2}$), cryogenic temperatures (operating near $T_{	ext{eff}} \approx 60 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The authors argue that conventional signatures ($	ext{I/O}$ curve) are insufficient, necessitating quantum measurements ($g^{(2)}$) for unambiguous proof of high-$ eta$ lasing.
figures_summary: Figures show $\mu	ext{PL}$ maps confirming mode confinement and spectral overlap; subsequent figures detail the power-dependent $g^{(2)}(	au)$ measurements showing the transition to Poissonian statistics, and the temporal broadening analysis.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from demonstrating basic exciton-cavity coupling via $\mu	ext{PL}$ (Fig. 2), establishing classical high-$ eta$ signatures ($	ext{I/O}$ curve) (Fig. 3), and finally providing definitive quantum verification through power-dependent photon autocorrelation measurements (Section 5).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the intersection of solid-state physics, cavity QED, and nonlinear optics by using layered materials to create highly controllable, integrated quantum light sources.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 All-vdW nanobeam cavity platform. a Schematic illustration of the WS2/MoSe2/WS2 heterostructure integrated into a photonic-crystal nanobeam cavity. The embedded MoSe2 ML pro- vides optical gain, while the surrounding multilayer WS2 simultaneously acts as the photonic cavity. b Three-dimensional FEM simulations of the dielectric-band cavity mode, showing the electric-field intensity distribution in the lateral (x–y) and vertical (y–z) planes together with the nanobeam geometry consisting of a taper and a mirror section. c Scanning electron microscopy image of a rep- resentative fabricated nanobeam cavity with a magnified view of the photonic-crystal region.

Fig. 2 Exciton-cavity coupling and directional emission in all-vdW nanobeam cavities. a Normalized temperature-dependent µPL map showing the spectral evolution of the neutral MoSe2 A- exciton (X) and cavity mode (C). The dotted lines represent fits to the extracted emission wavelengths (see Supplementary Section 6 for details on the fits). b Representative unnormalized spectra recorded at selected temperatures. c Real-space PL image recorded at the cavity resonance wavelength, show- ing resonant coupling into and propagation along the nanobeam. d Angle-resolved Fourier-space emission measured for linear polarizations oriented perpendicular and parallel to the nanobeam axis, respectively....
